question: Which of the five has been most explicit about serving mass-affluent clients, and what exactly have they said?

cells.label: fact

items.text: Schwab's Retail Investor business unit serves "a broad spectrum of individual investors, ranging from those just beginning their investing journey to clients with substantial and complex wealth management needs."
items.quote: Through the Retail Investor business unit, Schwab serves a broad spectrum of individual investors, ranging from those just beginning their investing journey to clients with substantial and complex wealth management needs.

items.text: Schwab offers Schwab Private Client Services for clients with $1 million to $10 million in qualifying assets, and Schwab Private Wealth Services for clients with more than $10 million.
items.quote: For clients with more substantial needs, Schwab Private Client Services™ (for clients with $1 million to $10 million in qualifying assets) and Schwab Private Wealth Services™ (for clients with more than $10 million) provide enhanced, relationship-based experiences

items.text: Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said clients can access financial planning, full-service advice, tax, trust, and estate services, and that the firm serves traders of all sophistication levels.
items.quote: With our wealth offer, clients can access financial planning, full-service advice, tax, trust, and estate services, tax-aware strategies, and more.

items.text: Schwab stated that 68% of affluent investors want and are willing to pay for advice.
items.quote: 68% of affluent investors want & are willing to pay for advice

items.text: Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said the firm is "expanding our branch footprint and hiring financial consultants and wealth consultants to serve even more of our higher net worth clients."
items.quote: In our retail business, we're expanding our branch footprint and hiring financial consultants and wealth consultants to serve even more of our higher net worth clients.

items.text: Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said about one-third of new clients are affluent, and Schwab is "winning with investors of all ages, wealth tiers, and time horizons."
items.quote: About one-third of new clients are affluent, and the volume of new trader clients continues to increase. To sum it up, we are winning with investors of all ages, wealth tiers, and time horizons.

items.text: Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab is "deepening relationships with our higher net worth clients by continuing to strengthen our alternatives offer."
items.quote: We're also deepening relationships with our higher net worth clients by continuing to strengthen our alternatives offer.

items.text: Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said the firm built out specialty teams catering to the unique needs of higher net worth clients.
items.quote: We've improved our tax, trust, and estate capabilities, and we've built out specialty teams catering to the unique needs of our higher net worth clients.

items.text: Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab's own wealth offerings target its large retail client base, with clients often joining Schwab young and being offered wealth capability later as their life circumstances warrant.
items.quote: "People typically join Schwab at a young age," he said. "Then what we do is we give them incredible service... at that point, that's where we think it's the right time to offer a wealth capability if the client wants it, and their life circumstances suggest it would be the right thing for them."

items.text: Schwab said 61% of affluent clients ages 25 to 44 prefer to consolidate their wealth and banking relationships.
items.quote: 61% of affluent clients ages 25 to 44, so they prefer to consolidate their wealth and banking relationships.

items.text: Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab has some 30 million retail accounts with close to $7 trillion in retail assets looking for advice, and that its 400 branches serve Schwab retail clients seeking advice.
items.quote: "We've got 30 million-ish retail accounts with close to $7 trillion in retail assets looking for advice," Wurster said. "We want to service those clients."

cells.reason: Schwab has made multiple explicit statements about serving affluent and mass-affluent clients, including specific asset-tiered service offerings and percentage statistics.
